survey: A stylised navy anchor, seen from the front with a slight tilt, floating as an icon on a striped background. The ring sits on top of the shank and is seen almost face-on; it is a clean torus. The stock is a crossbar with a ball on each end. It goes through a collar on the upper shank and lies in the same plane as the arms. That is the usual icon convention, not an error. The shank runs down into a V-shaped crown, which splits into two curved arms with arrowhead flukes. The left arm and the right arm are near mirror images. A tan twisted rope loops through the bottom of the ring, goes down under the stock collar, then winds about two turns around the shank as a steady helix. It ends where the shank meets the crown. The metal parts are sound: the ring, stock, shank, crown and arms all join properly and nothing is missing or extra. The tool panel marks no thin parts or ends on the rope. These findings come from looking at the drawing itself.

errors.where: Top of the rope, between the ring and the stock collar
errors.what: The rope loops through the ring, and both strands run down into the collar on the left and right of the shank. Below the collar only one strand comes out, on the right, and then winds down. The other strand is lost under the collar. A tight collar also leaves no gap for a rope to pass between it and the shank.

errors.where: Bottom end of the rope, where the shank meets the crown, left of centre
errors.what: The last turn of the rope just runs into the crown and stops. There is no knot, no lashing and no free tail, so the rope is not tied to anything at this end and looks fused into the metal.

fix: Have the rope pass through the anchor's ring and tie it in a visible knot at the ring. A single rope then winds loosely around the shank in front of the crossbar, not under its collar, and ends in a short frayed tail that hangs freely beside the crown. The rope should have no hidden or vanishing ends.
